findings.issue_text: Authorization is too permissive: any attendee of a booking (isAttendee) can add arbitrary guests, triggering emails sent 'from' the organizer and calendar updates, creating a spam/spoofing vector since attendee emails are user-controlled at booking time
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a user must be BOTH admin AND owner; a team admin (but not owner) is incorrectly denied — should be ||
When eventType.teamId is null the code checks team id 0

Uniqueness is only enforced client-side: server schema has no uniqueness refine, and uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees, not duplicates within the guests array itself, so submitting the same email twice creates duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails/ICS entries

Email comparison is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS can be bypassed by changing casing, and an existing attendee foo@x.com can be re-added as FOO@x.com; emails should be normalized (lowercase/trim) before comparisons and storage

No transaction/atomicity: prisma.booking.update persists new attendees before updateCalendarAttendees runs; if the calendar update throws, guests are already saved and a retry fails with misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid error

EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) (the actor's credentials) instead of the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the update uses the wrong user's calendar credentials and will fail or target the wrong calendar; credentials should come from booking.user
No check of booking.status: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, sending 'Guests Added' emails and ICS REQUEST updates for events that no longer exist
No upper bound on guests array size in the schema: a single request can add hundreds of emails, fanning out into hundreds of outbound emails per attendee — a mail-bombing/DoS vector; add .max(N)

For seated event types, attendees are inserted directly into booking.attendees, bypassing seat-booking logic (seatsReferences/capacity tracking), which can overbook seats and produce inconsistent attendee state

Read-then-write race: two concurrent addGuests calls both load the booking's attendees before either writes, so the same guest can be added twice; no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no transaction/serializable isolation

prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }): if booking.userId is null, a query for id 0 throws a raw Prisma error (unhandled → HTTP 500) instead of a proper TRPCError with a meaningful message

Email failures are swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'): the error object isn't logged, the project logger isn't used, and the API still returns success so the UI shows 'Guests added' even when no emails were sent

isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog is never reset on successful submit or when the dialog is closed/reopened via the overlay (only Cancel resets it), so the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error reappears on next open

No tests added for the new handler: authorization matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner/unrelated user), duplicate/blacklist filtering, seated bookings, and cancelled-booking rejection are all untested

handleAdd silently returns when the email list is empty, giving no feedback that nothing happened; the Zod schema is also redefined inline in the component instead of importing the shared server schema, risking drift between client and server validation

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization is too permissive: any attendee of a booking (isAttendee) can add arbitrary guests, triggering emails sent 'from' the organizer and calendar updates, creating a spam/spoofing vector since attendee emails are user-controlled at booking time

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes any authenticated user whose `user.email` matches any booking attendee (`isAttendee`) to add guests: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`. Once authorized, it updates calendar attendees (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) and sends emails/invites via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, where the organizer/attendee email templates set `from`/`replyTo` based on the organizer (`from: `${this.calEvent.organizer.name} <...>` / replyTo organizer email). There is no additional restriction limiting this action to the organizer/admin, so a normal attendee can add arbitrary guest email addresses and trigger outbound email/calendar updates appearing to come from the organizer, which is a plausible spam/spoofing vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a user must be BOTH admin AND owner; a team admin (but not owner) is incorrectly denied — should be ||
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same permission logic bug: using && requires both admin and owner, but permission should be granted if either is true (use ||).

adjudication_records.issue_text: When eventType.teamId is null the code checks team id 0

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed by calling `isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)` and `isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)`. If `booking.eventType?.teamId` is `null/undefined`, this explicitly passes `0` as the teamId, meaning the permission check is performed against team id `0` rather than being skipped/handled as “no team”. This is a concrete behavior in the diff and can lead to incorrect authorization semantics (at minimum unnecessary/incorrect lookup; potentially allowing/denying based on a non-real team id).

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying flaw: blacklist entries are lowercased but input/other comparisons are case-sensitive, so attackers can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS by using uppercase variants (and similarly re-add existing attendees). adjudication_records.issue_text: No transaction/atomicity: prisma.booking.update persists new attendees before updateCalendarAttendees runs; if the calendar update throws, guests are already saved and a retry fails with misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuestsHandler`, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no transaction or error handling around that call. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will fail but the DB write has already happened, leaving attendees added in Cal.com while the external calendar may not be updated. On a retry, `booking` is re-fetched including those newly-added attendees, so `uniqueGuests` becomes empty and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading in this scenario (the emails are now duplicates due to the prior partial success).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) (the actor's credentials) instead of the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the update uses the wrong user's calendar credentials and will fail or target the wrong calendar; credentials should come from booking.user

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, access control explicitly allows non-organizers (team admin/owner and attendees) to add guests. However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, where `user` is the actor from `ctx`, not the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `booking.user`). Since the event being updated belongs to the booking/organizer context (and the diff even loads `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them), using the actor’s credentials will either fail (attendee/admin lacks organizer calendar access) or update the wrong calendar. The diff therefore introduces a real correctness issue when someone other than the organizer adds guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check of booking.status: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, sending 'Guests Added' emails and ICS REQUEST updates for events that no longer exist

adjudication.rationale: In the added `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched and then attendees are appended and emails/calendar updates are sent without any check on a `status`/`cancelled`/`rejected` field. However, the diff does not show that `booking.status` exists on the `booking` model, nor does it show any established invariant that adding guests must be disallowed for non-active bookings. The finding assumes specific booking lifecycle states and intended behavior that are not verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on guests array size in the schema: a single request can add hundreds of emails, fanning out into hundreds of outbound emails per attendee — a mail-bombing/DoS vector; add .max(N)

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or other size limit). The handler `addGuestsHandler` then (1) `createMany` inserts all `uniqueGuests` as attendees and (2) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, where `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and enqueues an email per attendee (plus organizer/team emails). This makes a single request capable of triggering a large number of outbound emails and work proportional to the array size, which is a plausible mail-bombing/DoS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For seated event types, attendees are inserted directly into booking.attendees, bypassing seat-booking logic (seatsReferences/capacity tracking), which can overbook seats and produce inconsistent attendee state

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new rows to `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (which is explicitly carried into the `CalendarEvent` object later). For seated/limited-capacity event types, this bypasses any capacity/seat-allocation enforcement and can add more attendees than there are seats, leading to an overbooked booking and inconsistent state versus whatever seat/capacity logic exists elsewhere. This defect is directly observable in the diff because there is no guard or seat-tracking update before inserting attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read-then-write race: two concurrent addGuests calls both load the booking's attendees before either writes, so the same guest can be added twice; no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no transaction/serializable isolation

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a read (findFirst include attendees) and then a write (booking.update with attendees.createMany) with duplicate filtering performed only in application code based on the earlier read. That is a TOCTOU pattern and could race under concurrent calls. However, the finding’s key claim (“the same guest can be added twice; no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email)”) is not verifiable from this diff: the Prisma schema/DB constraints are not shown, and Prisma can also enforce uniqueness via a unique index (which would cause one call to fail rather than create duplicates). Since the duplicate-rows outcome depends on constraints not present in the diff, the finding as stated is not strictly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }): if booking.userId is null, a query for id 0 throws a raw Prisma error (unhandled → HTTP 500) instead of a proper TRPCError with a meaningful message

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` without first ensuring `booking.userId` is non-null/non-undefined. If `booking.userId` is null (the code itself suggests this possibility by using `|| 0` and later `booking.userId || 0` elsewhere), the query becomes `id: 0`, which will not match a real user and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma “not found” error. That error is not caught and not converted to a `TRPCError`, so it would surface as an unhandled internal error (HTTP 500) rather than a meaningful TRPC error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failures are swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'): the error object isn't logged, the project logger isn't used, and the API still returns success so the UI shows 'Guests added' even when no emails were sent

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is ignored (not logged), `console.log` is used instead of any structured/project logger, and no error is rethrown. The handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless, so the client mutation `onSuccess` will run and show the success toast `t("guests_added")` even if email delivery failed. This behavior is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog is never reset on successful submit or when the dialog is closed/reopened via the overlay (only Cancel resets it), so the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error reappears on next open

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd`), but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. On successful mutation (`onSuccess`), the code closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Also, closing the dialog via the overlay/ESC triggers `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` and likewise does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Therefore, after an invalid attempt, reopening the dialog can show the stale "Emails must be unique and valid" error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests added for the new handler: authorization matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner/unrelated user), duplicate/blacklist filtering, seated bookings, and cancelled-booking rejection are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `addGuests` TRPC mutation/handler and related UI/email code, but it does not add or modify any test files. So it’s true that no tests were added in this change. However, “missing tests” is a process/coverage concern rather than a concrete, verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff itself (the finding also lists scenarios as “untested,” which is not directly provable from the diff alone without seeing the existing test suite).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleAdd silently returns when the email list is empty, giving no feedback that nothing happened; the Zod schema is also redefined inline in the component instead of importing the shared server schema, risking drift between client and server validation

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.handleAdd, the code explicitly `return`s when `multiEmailValue.length === 0` without setting any error state or showing a toast, so if the user removes all email fields (MultiEmail allows deleting entries via the “x” button until the array is empty) and clicks “Add”, nothing happens and no feedback is provided. Also, the client defines its own Zod schema inline (`z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`) rather than reusing the server’s input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts`; the two validations are already different (client enforces uniqueness; server schema does not), which is a real, verifiable risk of validation drift between client/server.
